title: Max builds a levee (the duck got in four times)

beats.text: A squirrel just blasted Max's rubber duck through his levee.
Rewind to a sunny day, when the river was low.
Max promised his kids a backyard that never floods. Sand wall, done!
The river rises, water slips between the sand grains, and the soaked wall slumps.
So Max adds a clay core; its tiny grains barely let water move, so the leak stops in the middle.
It holds, but water sneaks under, through buried sand, and pushes up. A sand boil! Sandbags, fast.
A heavy seepage berm holds the ground down. Relief wells bleed the pressure safely into a ditch.
Then a huge storm pours right over the top, and the waterfall scours the bare dirt.
That's how most Katrina levees failed. So Max raises the crest three feet above the hundred-year flood, plus grass and riprap.
Perfect, until a squirrel digs in. Floodwater follows, carries soil away, and the hole widens: piping.
Burrows average 8.2 metres. So Max mows short, inspects, and packs every hole shut.
Next storm, the yard stays dry, the kids bounce, and Max cheers. Which levee failure would you fix first?
